0.
0.1 This Indian

FOREWORD

Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 20 October 1986, after the draft finalized by the Shipbuilding Sectional Committee had been approved by the Marine, Cargo Movement and Packaging Division Council. 0.2 At present, the terminology for Ships' Side Scuttles and Rectangular Windows is covered in the following Indian Standards: i) IS : 5474( Part II )-1972 and types Ships' side scuttles: ordinary Ships'

Part II Terminology rectangular windows:

ii) IS : 8886 ( Part I )-1978 Ship Part I Types and dimensions

0.3 A need has been felt to prepare a unified standard covering vocabulary for Ships' side scuttles and windows. Earlier, the term " Ships' Windows " Ships' was used in connection with Ships' rectangular windows only. round windows ( Ships' side scuttles ) were not allotted to this term. Until now, a common main term was missing. With this standard, it is endeavoured amongst others, to introduce a common main term for all In the sense of this Standard the kinds of windows used in shipbuilding. term " Ships' Window " is applied as a collective term for windows of round shape ( Ships' side scuttles ) and for windows of angular shape ( also including sliding window, fan light window, wheelhouse window, etc ). 0.4 In the preparation of this vocabulary, care has been taken to standardize only suitable terms and definitions and not to perpetuate unsuitable The illustrations given against the terms because of their use in the past. respective terms are simp!ified or symbolic representations given in order to facilitate the comprehension. They serve only as means and example and do not confine the construction. 0.5 Where more than one term was usual for the relevant definition, only a single term has been chosen, in general the most common one, for the sake of unambiguity.

5. TERMS Cl Jvo.

FOR GLASS PANES Term Figure

5.1

Glass pane

A flat piece of glass cut or edge-worked to size and shape ready for glazing. In special cases the pane may be composed of two or more glass panes or be made of other transparent material ( for example, acrylic sheet )

L

5.2

Heated glass pane

Two or more glass panes, laminated and bonded together with an electrical heating element between them to ensure unrestricted vision in frost and snow conditions
glass NOTE - Heated used on ships panesare principaliy for the windows of wheelhollses and bridges and also in enclosed locations used for lock-out and manoeuvring purposes

go.
5.3

Term

*

Dejinition

Figure

Fire resistant glass pane

A glass pane, consisting of two or more glass panes and one or more interwhich mediate layers consist of a gas, a transparent plastic or other transparent any material Glass which, if fractured, gives fragments, which are less liable to cause severe cuts than fragments of ordinary glass NOTE- Laminated and wired glasses are referred to as types of safety glass

5.4

Safety

glass

c N

5.5

Toughened safety glass

Glass which has been converted to safety glass by subjection to a process of heating and rapid cooling, so that, if fractured, it disintegrates into small pieces and, in addition, its liability to fracture under the action of external forces or changes of temperature is greatly reduced

Cl
Jvo. 5.6

l-ml Plate glass

Dejhition
Transparent soda-limesilica glasses produced by floating molten glass on a bath of molten metal thus creating flat parallel and polished surfaces

Figure

5.7

Sheet glass

w'

Transparent soda-limesilica glass obtained by vertical continuous drawing thus creating fine polished surfaces

5.8

Wired glass

Soda-lime-silica glass, having metal wires ( for example, spot welded square mesh) introduced and compeltely embedded during rolling, the structure of which remains largely held together if the glass fractures ( cast and polished )
